title: The two-term resolution of the finite coefficient sheaves
statement:
Let $E/\Ql$ be finite with uniformizer $\pi_E$ and $n\geq1$. For every scheme $X$
the sequence of $\mathcal O_{E,X}$-module sheaves on $X_{\Proet}$

$$
0\to\mathcal O_{E,X}\xrightarrow{\ \pi_E^n\ }\mathcal O_{E,X}\to(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_X\to0
$$

is exact. Consequently, for $K\in D(X_{\Proet},\mathcal O_E)$,
$K_n=K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{E,X}}(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_X$ is
isomorphic to the cone of $\pi_E^n\colon K\to K$, naturally in $K$, and for
$1\leq m\leq n$ there are triangles
$K_m\xrightarrow{\pi_E^{n}}K_{n+m}\to K_n\to$, in particular
$K_1\to K_{n+1}\to K_n\to$.

proof.text: Put $A=\mathcal O_E$, $a=\pi_E$ and $B_r=A/a^rA$. The absolute-value/subspace topology is that of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], $A$ is a subring of $E$, $a\ne0$, and $0<|a|<1$. In particular multiplication by $a^r$ is injective, and division by $a^r$ on $a^rA$ is continuous: it is restriction of multiplication by the fixed element $a^{-r}$ of the topological field $E$, with values in the subspace $A$. The ordinary augmented complex $[A\xrightarrow{a^r}A]\to B_r[0]$ is a finite free resolution, and $B_r$ is a finite set, by [lem-weil-pbc-standard-quotients-perfect]. The quotient topology on $B_r$ is discrete. Indeed, if $|x|<|a|^r$, then $|x/a^r|<1$, so $x\in a^rA$; hence $a^rA$ contains a neighbourhood of zero and is open (translate that neighbourhood at each of its points). Every coset is open, which is the assertion of discreteness. These observations hold for every $r\ge1$.

source.place: On the point: topology, injectivity and finite quotients

proof.text: For every profinite set $S$, [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] identifies sections of $\underline A$ and $\underline{B_r}$ with $C(S,A)$ and $C(S,B_r)$. Multiplication by $a^r$ is injective on sections. If $f:S\to A$ reduces to zero, the quotient $s\mapsto a^{-r}f(s)$ is continuous by step 1 and is the unique section mapping to $f$. Given $g:S\to B_r$, choose a lift $b_t\in A$ of each of its finitely many values $t$; its fibres are open and closed, and the function equal to $b_t$ on $g^{-1}(t)$ is a continuous lift. Thus the section sequence is short exact for every $S$, including the empty set. It follows that $0\to\underline A\xrightarrow{a^r}\underline A\to\underline{B_r}\to0$ is short exact as abelian sheaves: kernels are sectionwise and the cokernel is the sheafification of the sectionwise cokernel, by [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact]. All maps are $\underline A$-linear for pointwise operations.

source.place: On the point: the three sectionwise exactness checks

proof.text: Here is the precise exact-pullback input, replacing the nonexistent imported module-exactness citation. Use small site models in a universe below that of the coefficient sheaves. In [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point], $u:*_{\mathrm{proet}}\to(\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z)_{\mathrm{proet}}$ preserves finite limits and coverings, and $p_X^*=\pi_X^*p^*$, where $p^*$ is sheafified left Kan extension along $u^{op}$. Profinite sets have finite limits (the closed inverse-image subsets giving finite products and equalizers), so [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor], Tag 00X6, applies to $u$ and makes $p^*$ exact on abelian sheaves. The other factor $\pi_X^*$ is exact by [lem-sfb-finite-upper-star-exact]. Hence $p_X^*$ preserves the short exact sequence of step 2. Its strong monoidal structure transports the scalar actions, and [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] identifies the resulting ring and quotient with $R=A_X$ and $B_{r,X}$. The maps remain multiplication by $a^r$ and reduction, since their scalar-action diagrams are the images of the original diagrams under this monoidal functor. For these essentially small sites, [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-tensor-closed], applied to abelian groups, supplies exact sheafification and its strong symmetric monoidal structure, including tensor stability of its local equivalences; thus the sheafification hypotheses of the following equivalence hold. Internal modules may be read as sectionwise module sheaves via [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence], with underlying sheaves unchanged; [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] computes their kernels sectionwise and cokernels by sheafification. Thus underlying abelian exactness proves exactly the asserted short exact sequence of $R$-modules. No constant/completed coefficient identification or invertibility of $\ell$ on $X$ is used.

source.place: On X: exact inverse image and transported coefficient actions

proof.text: Let $P_r$ be the complex with $R$ in degrees $-1,0$, differential $a^r$, and augmentation the reduction $R\to B_{r,X}$ in degree zero. Step 3 says $H^{-1}(P_r)=0$, $H^0(P_r)=B_{r,X}$, and all its other cohomology sheaves vanish, so its augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism. Its terms are free of rank one, and are flat: $R\otimes_R M\to M$, $b\otimes m\mapsto bm$, has inverse $m\mapsto1\otimes m$, hence tensor by $R$ is the identity functor and is exact, as required by [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-independent-bounded-flat-kflat], Tag 06YQ, to this bounded-above flat complex on the essentially small pro-etale site. It is K-flat. This establishes the actual sheaf resolution rather than treating the ordinary $A$-module resolution as a sheaf theorem.

source.place: On X: the augmented rank-one free resolution is K-flat

proof.text: Use the layer-B notation of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]: $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E)=D(\Mod_{\mathcal O_{E,X}})$ for the pulled-back condensed ring, rather than the constant-ring notation in the site definition. For an arbitrary, possibly unbounded $K$, choose a K-flat flat-term representative $C$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The two-variable model and descent statement [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] computes $P_r\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}K$ by $\operatorname{Tot}(P_r\otimes_R C)$. Since $P_r\simeq B_{r,X}[0]$, the model for $K_r=K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}B_{r,X}$ is $\operatorname{Tot}(C\otimes_RP_r)$. The interchange $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{pq}y\otimes x$ for $x\in C^p$, $y\in P_r^q$ is a chain isomorphism from this complex to $\operatorname{Tot}(P_r\otimes_RC)$: it is balanced because $R$ is commutative, and substituting in the total differential gives the same signs on both sides. Its inverse is the same signed interchange. Thus the latter complex computes precisely $K_r$. The degree-$q$ term is $C^q\oplus C^{q+1}$ after the unit identifications $R\otimes_R C^j=C^j$; the differential is $(x,y)\mapsto(d_Cx+a^ry,-d_Cy)$, directly from [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], because the first-factor degree of the second summand is $-1$. This is the cone differential of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] for $a^r:C\to C$. The identification commutes with every chain map $C\to C'$: it is the identity on these two summands. The tensor-model descent and uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] therefore extend these identifications to a natural isomorphism in $K$; the cone here means this fixed two-term tensor/cone model, not a choice of a cone made separately for each morphism in a triangulated category.

source.place: On X: compute the derived reduction and its natural cone model

proof.text: For $m,n\ge1$ consider $i:B_m\to B_{n+m}$, $[x]\mapsto[a^nx]$, and $q:B_{n+m}\to B_n$, $[y]\mapsto[y]$. These are $A$-linear. Changing $x$ by $a^mz$ changes $a^nx$ by $a^{n+m}z$, so $i$ is well defined. If $a^nx=a^{n+m}z$ in $A\subset E$, cancel the nonzero $a^n$ to get $x=a^mz$, proving injectivity. The kernel of $q$ consists exactly of classes $[a^nx]$, and $q$ is surjective by choosing a representative in $A$. This gives $0\to B_m\xrightarrow{i}B_{n+m}\xrightarrow{q}B_n\to0$. For a profinite $S$, a continuous function into any of these finite discrete rings is locally constant. A function to $B_n$ lifts along $q$ by choosing one value above each value of the function; a function to $B_{n+m}$ in its kernel has a unique locally constant preimage under $i$, since the image is finite discrete. Hence the condensed sequence is sectionwise short exact just as in step 2. Applying the exact $p_X^*$ established in step 3 gives $0\to B_{m,X}\xrightarrow{i_X}B_{n+m,X}\xrightarrow{q_X}B_{n,X}\to0$. This computation uses only cancellation and the finite discrete topology already proved; it does not invoke a separate quotient-power lemma.

source.place: Triangles: explicit quotient-power maps, kernel and surjectivity

proof.text: Place the last sequence of step 6 in degree zero. By [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle], Tag 0152, it gives a distinguished triangle $B_{m,X}\to B_{n+m,X}\to B_{n,X}\to B_{m,X}[1]$ in $D(R)$. Tensor by $K$ preserves this triangle: choose the K-flat representative of step 5 and apply [lem-sc-source-kflat-tensor-left-triangulated] to the abelian monoidal category of $R$-modules, with its sheaf relative tensor and K-flat derived tensor model from [def-sfb-derived-tensor-modules] and [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. The required flat-term resolving localization is exactly the equivalence in the latter statement, so no boundedness of $K$ or enough-projectives hypothesis is needed. The three vertices identify with $K_m,K_{n+m},K_n$, and the two arrows are $1_K\otimes^{\mathbf L}i_X$ and $1_K\otimes^{\mathbf L}q_X$. Thus the notation $\pi_E^n$ on the first arrow means the map induced by $[x]\mapsto[\pi_E^nx]$ between the two different coefficient quotients. Restrict to $1\le m\le n$ as in the statement and then put $m=1$ to obtain the final displayed triangle.
